indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B3.2.1.3: Show understanding of the roles of condensation, evaporation, transpiration and precipitation in the hydrological (water) cycle
indicator.objective: Identify the types of precipitation (rain, snow, hail, sleet) and describe the differences among them

skills.description: Match a description to the correct type of precipitation
Give examples of when each type might occur

misconceptions: Snow and hail are the same thing.
It snows in Ghana all the time.

questions.stem: Which of these is a type of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Rain is a common type of precipitation that falls from clouds.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think wind is precipitation.

questions.stem: Which of these falls as small hard pieces of ice during a storm?
hints: It is ice that falls like stones.
questions.explanation: Hail is precipitation in the form of small, hard balls of ice that fall during thunderstorms.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse hail with snow.

questions.stem: What is the main difference between rain and snow?
options: Rain is liquid water and snow is soft white ice crystals
Rain is cold and snow is hot
Rain falls up and snow falls down
hints: What happens to rain when it hits the ground?
questions.explanation: Rain is liquid water, while snow is frozen water vapour that forms soft, white ice crystals.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think they are identical.

questions.stem: What type of precipitation is most common in Ghana?
hints: It happens during the wet season.
questions.explanation: Rain is the most common type of precipitation in Ghana because of its tropical climate.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think snow falls in Ghana.

options: Ice pellets or a mixture of rain and snow
hints: It falls like rain but is icy.
questions.explanation: Sleet is precipitation consisting of ice pellets or a mixture of rain and snow.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think sleet is just heavy rain.

questions.stem: Which type of precipitation consists of soft, white ice crystals?
hints: It falls in very cold places.
questions.explanation: Snow is made of soft, white ice crystals.
questions.misconception: Pupils may match this description to hail.

questions.stem: How is hail different from snow?
options: Hail is hard ice pellets, while snow is soft ice crystals
Hail is soft and snow is hard
Hail is liquid and snow is solid
hints: Hail can hurt if it hits you.
questions.explanation: Hail is made of hard ice pellets, while snow consists of soft ice crystals.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think hail and snow are identical.

questions.stem: Which type of precipitation is liquid water drops falling from clouds?
questions.explanation: Rain consists of liquid water drops falling from clouds.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think it is sleet.

questions.stem: When is hail most likely to occur?
hints: There is usually thunder and lightning.
questions.explanation: Hail forms in strong thunderstorm clouds (cumulonimbus clouds) when updrafts carry raindrops high where it is freezing.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think hail occurs on sunny days.

questions.stem: In which type of climate would you expect to see snow?
questions.explanation: Snow occurs in very cold climates where the temperature in the clouds is below freezing.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think snow occurs in hot climates.

questions.explanation: Common types of precipitation include rain, snow, hail, and sleet.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name non-precipitation items like wind.

questions.stem: What is the difference between rain and hail?
answer: rain is liquid water, hail is hard ice pellets
questions.explanation: Rain is liquid water, while hail is hard ice pellets.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think hail is just frozen rain.

questions.stem: Ama says 'Sleet is just heavy rain.' Is she right?
options: No, sleet contains ice pellets or a mix of rain and snow
hints: Does sleet feel like rain or ice?
questions.explanation: Ama is not right. Sleet is not just heavy rain; it contains ice pellets or a mixture of rain and snow.
questions.misconception: Pupils may simplify sleet as heavy rain.

questions.stem: Why does snow fall in some countries but not in Ghana?
options: Because those countries are much colder, so the water freezes in the clouds
Because Ghana is closer to the moon
Because snow only falls on mountains
questions.explanation: Snow forms when water freezes in cold clouds. Countries that have very cold temperatures at cloud level experience snow, while Ghana's tropical climate is too warm.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think snow is random.

questions.stem: Explain the difference between rain, snow, and hail.

criteria.description: States snow is soft ice crystals and hail is hard ice pellets

questions.explanation: Rain is liquid. Snow is soft ice crystals. Hail is hard ice pellets.

questions.stem: Name the four main types of precipitation and briefly describe one.
questions.explanation: The four types are rain, snow, hail, and sleet.

questions.stem: A farmer hears thunder and sees dark clouds. It starts to rain, but soon hard ice pellets start falling. What type of precipitation is this?
questions.explanation: The hard ice pellets falling during a thunderstorm are hail.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse it with sleet (which is softer and mixed with rain).

questions.stem: Why is it dangerous to walk outside during a heavy hailstorm?
options: Hailstones can be hard and large enough to cause injury
questions.explanation: Hailstones can be hard and large, and falling ice can cause injuries to people and damage to property.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think hail is harmless like snow.

questions.stem: Show your teacher how you can create 'artificial rain' in the classroom (e.g., using a watering can or a sieve with water).

criteria.description: Performs the activity to simulate rain
Explains that the water drops represent rain

hints: Let the water fall like drops.
questions.explanation: This demonstrates the concept of rain as liquid drops falling from above.
